subject: maths
title: Numbers to 120: Count, Order and Compare Numbers
seo_title: Year 1 Numbers to 120 Maths Worksheets: Count, Order and Compare, Free with Answer Key
standard_text: Recognise, represent and order numbers to at least 120 using physical and virtual materials, numerals, number lines and charts
meta_desc: Free Year 1 numbers to 120 maths worksheets for the Australian Curriculum: count objects and bundles of ten, numbers before, after and between, ordering numbers, number lines and the 120 chart, and comparing with more and fewer. 100 picture questions with an answer key.
key_big: Count on by ones. After 99 comes 100, then 101, 102, 103 … 110.
key_sub: One hundred and two is written 102, not 1002. To compare, look at the tens first: 71 is bigger than 17.
body_html:
Numbers to 120 follow a pattern

Count on by ones. Only the ones digit changes until you get to 9. Then 1 more makes a new ten. After 99 comes 100. Then the pattern starts again: 101, 102, 103 …

Count onWhat happens
37, 38, 39, 409 ones and 1 more make a new ten
97, 98, 99, 10010 tens make one hundred
100, 101, 102After 100 comes 101, not 110
107, 108, 109, 110100 and 1 more ten

Count in tens, then ones

Put things in rows or bundles of 10. Count the tens first. Then count on the ones.

Write the number

How do you write “one hundred and two”?

It is 100 and 2 more. There are no tens, so the tens digit is 0.

Answer: 102 (not 1002)

Before, after and between

After is 1 more. Before is 1 less. Between is the number in the middle.

The 120 chart and number lines

Each row of the 120 chart has 10 numbers. Go right for 1 more. Go down for 10 more.

Order and compare

A number with 3 digits is bigger than a number with 2 digits. For 2-digit numbers, look at the tens first.

Which is bigger?

17 or 71?

17 has 1 ten. 71 has 7 tens. 7 tens is more.

Answer: 71

Order from smallest to biggest

102, 99, 110

99 has only 2 digits, so it is the smallest. 102 comes before 110.

Answer: 99, 102, 110

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Writing 1002 for one hundred and twoWrite 102. The 0 means no tens
Reading 17 as 71Read the tens digit first: 17 is 1 ten and 7 ones
Counting 98, 99, 100, 110After 100 comes 101, then 102 … 110
Writing 310 after 399 ones and 1 more make a new ten: 40
Thinking 99 is bigger than 1023 digits beat 2 digits: 102 is bigger

faq.q: What numbers should a Year 1 student know in Australia?
faq.a: The Australian Curriculum asks Year 1 students to recognise, represent and order numbers to at least 120. They count objects, read and write numerals, and use number lines and charts.

faq.q: Why does my child write 1002 for one hundred and two?
faq.a: They write 100 and then 2, just as they hear it. Show 10 bundles of 10 and 2 more sticks, then point out that 102 has only three digits and the 0 means no tens.
It is a chart with the numbers 1 to 120 in rows of 10. Moving right is 1 more and moving down is 10 more, so it helps students count past 100 and find missing numbers.

faq.q: How can I help my child count past 100 at home?
faq.a: Count real things in tens and ones, like bundles of icy pole sticks or pegs. Practise the tricky spots out loud: 99, 100, 101 and 109, 110, 111.

items.q: Which number is this?
items.e: One hundred and two is 100 and 2 more. Write 102. The 0 shows there are no tens. Do not write 1002.

items.q: How do you say this number?

items.q: What number comes after 9?
items.e: Count on 1 from 9: 9, 10. 8 comes before 9.

items.q: What number comes just before 12?
items.e: Count back 1 from 12: 12, 11. 13 comes after 12.

items.q: What number comes between 16 and 18?

items.q: What number comes after 14?

items.q: What number comes just before 20?
items.e: Count back 1 from 20: 20, 19. Not 29: going back 1 from 20 goes down a ten.

items.q: What number comes after 29?

What number comes after 39?
items.e: After 39 comes 40. 3 tens become 4 tens. Do not write 310.

items.q: What number comes just before 50?

items.q: What number comes after 68?

items.q: What number comes just before 81?

items.q: What number comes after 99?

items.q: What number comes between 99 and 101?

items.q: Put the cards in order from smallest to biggest. Which number is second?

items.q: Put the cards in order from biggest to smallest.
items.e: Biggest first. 58 is the biggest, then 55, then 50. 49 has only 4 tens. The order is 58, 55, 50, 49.

items.q: Which number fits between 45 and 61?
items.e: The number must be bigger than 45 and smaller than 61. 54 is 5 tens and 4 ones. 54 fits. 64 is too big. 41 and 16 are too small.

items.q: Which number is the biggest?
items.e: 99 has big digits, but it is only 2 digits. 102 has 3 digits: 1 hundred. 102 comes after 100. 102 is the biggest.

items.q: Which number is the smallest?

items.q: Put the cards in order from smallest to biggest.

items.e: Numbers with 3 digits are bigger. 117 is more than 107. Then 71, then 17. The order is 117, 107, 71, 17.

items.q: Put the cards in order from smallest to biggest.
items.e: 11 has only 2 digits, so it is the smallest. 101 comes before 110. The order is 11, 101, 110.

items.q: Apples for recess. Which row has the fewest apples?
items.e: Count each row: A has 8, B has 7, C has 10, D has 5. Row D has 5. That is the fewest.

items.q: Which is true?
items.e: 14 is 1 ten and 4 ones. 41 is 4 tens and 1 one. So 41 is more than 14.

items.q: Which row has more than 10 balls?
items.e: Count each row: A has 12, B has 9, C has 10, D has 8. Row A has 12. That is the only row with more than 10.

items.q: Grace has 3 bundles of 10 icy pole sticks and 6 more sticks. How many sticks?
items.e: Count the bundles by tens: 10, 20, 30. Then count on: 31, 32, 33, 34, 35, 36. There are 36 sticks.

items.q: These cards show stickers. Who has the fewest stickers?
items.e: Look at the tens first. 13 has only 1 ten. Do not read 13 as 31. The smallest number is 13. William has the fewest.

items.q: These cards show how many shells each child found at the beach. Who found the most shells?
items.e: Look at the tens first. 42 has 4 tens and 2 ones. 40 has 4 tens and 0 ones. The biggest number is 42. Harper has the most.

items.q: The class has 26 students. There are 30 chairs. How many more chairs than students?
items.e: Count on from 26 to 30: 27, 28, 29, 30. That is 4 jumps. There are 4 more chairs. Do not add: 26 and 30 is 56.

items.q: Sienna has 59 footy cards. Her friend has 1 more. How many cards does the friend have?
items.e: 1 more than 59 is 60. 9 ones and 1 more make a new ten. Do not write 510.

items.q: Each Year 1 class counted the books it read. Which class read the fewest books?
items.e: 50 and 58 have the fewest tens: 5 tens. 50 has 0 ones. 50 is the smallest. 1C read the fewest.

items.q: Which is true?
items.e: 99 comes just before 100. 102 comes after 100. So 102 is more than 99.

items.q: The class counts the days of school. Today is day 100. What day was yesterday?
items.e: Yesterday is 1 day before. 1 less than 100 is 99. 101 is tomorrow.

items.q: These cards show pages read this term. Who read the most pages?
items.e: 99 has big digits, but it has only 2 digits. 102 is 1 hundred and 2 more. 102 comes after 100. The biggest number is 102. Liam has the most.

items.q: There are 100 people at the sausage sizzle. 10 more come. How many people are there now?
items.e: 10 more than 100 is 110. 100 is 10 tens. 1 more ten makes 110. 101 is only 1 more.

items.q: Mia counts shells on the beach: 98, 99, 100. Her friend says the next number is 110. What is the right number?
items.e: After 100 comes 101. Count on by ones: 100, 101, 102 … 110 comes later.

items.q: The school canteen has 108 icy poles. It sells 1. How many are left?
items.e: 1 less than 108 is 107. 109 is 1 more. Write 107, not 1007.

items.q: The school houses got points at the athletics carnival. Which house has the most points?
items.e: 107 has 3 digits: 1 hundred and 7 more. It is the biggest. Yellow has the most. 71 is less than 100.
